title: The $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Index of a Pair of Pure States and the Topology of Interacting 1D Superconductors
abstract: We define a relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$-index $\mathcal{N}(ω_1,ω_2)$ for locally-comparable, parity-invariant pure states on a unital $C^*$-algebra. We prove that the index is well-defined, multiplicative, invariant under parity-preserving automorphisms, and locally constant in the norm topology. For the one-dimensional self-dual CAR algebra, we apply this construction to the half-chain automorphism $σ$ and define the many-body Majorana number $\mathcal{N}σ(ω):=\mathcal{N}(ω,ω\circσ)$ for parity-invariant $σ$-local pure states. In the quasi-free Hilbert--Schmidt regime, this index agrees with the usual single-body Majorana number. We then introduce symmetric local automorphism paths and prove that $\mathcal{N}_σ$ completely classifies the resulting automorphic-path-components. This automorphic-path equivalence retains the bulk Majorana number but may forget a relative zero-dimensional parity obstruction.
summary: This work introduces a relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$-index to characterize pairs of pure states on $C^*$-algebras relevant to 1D superconductors. By applying this index to the self-dual CAR algebra, the authors show that the resulting Majorana number completely classifies the topological components of the system's ground states. This provides a rigorous mathematical tool for understanding topological order in low-dimensional quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper defines and studies a relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$-index, $\mathcal{N}(\omega_1, \omega_2)$, for pairs of pure states on a $C^*$-algebra, relating it to topological invariants in condensed matter systems.
main_result: The index $\mathcal{N}_\sigma(\omega)$ completely classifies the automorphic-path-components of states in the 1D self-dual CAR algebra, capturing the bulk Majorana number.
method: The authors use algebraic methods involving $C^*$-algebras, GNS representations, and the construction of relative indices derived from parity-invariant pure states.
model_or_system: The primary model is the one-dimensional self-dual CAR algebra, used to describe interacting 1D superconductors. The analysis focuses on pure states ($\omega$) defined on this algebra.
key_observables: The relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$-index $\mathcal{N}(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ and the many-body Majorana number $\mathcal{N}_\sigma(\omega)$.
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in the quasi-free Hilbert--Schmidt regime, and the index is sensitive to parity-preserving automorphisms.
main_assumptions: The index is proven to be locally constant in the norm topology but not weak-$\ast$-continuous, and the classification by $\mathcal{N}_\sigma$ may forget a zero-dimensional parity obstruction.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$-index and proves its fundamental properties (well-defined, multiplicative). It then applies this to the 1D self-dual CAR algebra to define the Majorana number, culminating in the classification theorem based on automorphic-path equivalence.
why_interesting: The index provides a powerful topological invariant that classifies the ground state structure of 1D superconductors, linking algebraic topology ($\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants) directly to physical properties like Majorana zero modes.
